	<p><em style="font-size: 16px;">“As an artist, I look to bring awareness to these issues by transporting viewers with paintings that portray the splendor of what we stand to lose by our inaction.”</em><span style="font-size: 16px;"> – Leslie Wayne</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 16px;"><b><br />
Leslie Wayne's </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">new exhibition, </span><b>The Unintended Blues,</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> documents rising sea levels through aerial landscape paintings of vulnerable US shorelines and melting icebergs in the Arctic Circle. Additional multi-media piece engage viewers with issues around present day climate science. In these works, Wayne captures the beauty of our natural environment and renders with graphic clarity one of our greatest existential threats.</span></span></p>
<p><strong><span style="font-size: 16px;">The exhibition in the Upper Gallery at the Arts Center at Governors Island runs from July 24-September 27, Fridays-Sunday 12-5pm.</span></strong></p>
<p><strong><span style="font-size: 16px;">Free and accessible to all. </span></strong></p>

	<h5><span style="font-weight: 400; font-size: 16px;"><strong>Leslie Wayne</strong> is an artist whose work lies at the intersection of abstraction and representation. While she’s most known for her highly dimensional abstract paintings based on geology, her recent aerial landscapes conjure up deep questions about the American landscape, its mythologies and the environment. Wayne has exhibited nationally and internationally, and her work is in numerous public collections. She has received awards from the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation, Joan Mitchell Foundation, Francis J. Greenburger Foundation, Pollock Krasner Foundation, NYSCA, and NYFA, among others. She is represented by Jack Shainman Gallery.</span></h5>

<p style="text-align: right;">- Leslie Wayne</p>
